item.title: 5 questions parents may have after Trump's latest vaccine move
item.description: Parents may be confused about the status of vaccines for their kids after President Trump's new executive order. It's important to know nothing is changing right away.

item.title: A midwife crosses 'maternity deserts' to make a difference for Black moms and babies
item.description: New research from the March of Dimes says more than half of U.S. counties have no labor and delivery hospitals. One Black midwife tries to make a difference for moms in Alabama.

item.title: Hunter Biden says Joe Biden's cancer has spread. A doctor explains what that means
item.description: Former President Joe Biden's cancer has spread to his bones, according to his son Hunter. NPR's A Martinez asks Johns Hopkins Professor Otis Brawley about prostate cancer diagnoses and treatments.

item.title: Trump and RFK Jr. try again to upend vaccines for kids
item.description: President Trump signed an executive order on Monday about vaccines, saying children should get fewer. His administration has been blocked in the courts from changing the vaccine schedule.

item.title: People with disabilities say Medicaid income limits can stifle career advancement
item.description: Medicaid will have new work requirements next year. But some people with disabilities, who already work, say they'd like to work more, but risk losing their Medicaid coverage if they earn too much.

item.title: It's been a record summer for foodborne illness
item.description: Heat and tainted produce have made this a record summer for foodborne illness. Cases of cyclosporiasis have topped 10,000, and the CDC just traced a new salmonella outbreak to Mexican jalapeños.
